Settlement locks full delivery and custody rowsets, requires resolved deliveries, calculates expectation from Collected, and posts actual positive remit to Main. Strong existing delivery/custody locks and idempotency retained; this finding concerns wrong monetary basis, not missing same-driver settlement locking.

findings.title: First stock receipt can race unit-change admission and reinterpret movement history

source_evidence.trigger: Initially valid inventory item with UnitA and no stock movements. Authorized inventory_manage update requests distinct UnitB. Separately authorized purchasing receipt for same existing item uses positive quantity/cost, credit payment0, valid supplier/open day, fresh IDs.
schedule: UpdateInventory loads item81 and checks unitChanged84, then StockMovements.Any87 returnsfalse and Domain guard88 accepts; pause before Save100.

ReceivePurchase commits a legitimate PurchaseReceipt In movement with quantity milliunits in previously current UnitA: stock167-175, Save207/Commit208. Choose complete receipt before metadata writer resumes, so transactions need not overlap.
UpdateInventory resumes sets UnitB93 and Save100; no repeated movement query, transaction-held inventory anchor or version token.
source_evidence.root_cause: Immutable-unit predicate is evaluated before write without coordinating the first stock-movement admission. InventoryItem mapping244 is primary key only, no concurrency token; movement FK protects existence, not unit interpretation.
source_evidence.impact: Historical bare milliunit movement is reinterpreted under UnitB, contrary explicit InventoryRules40-47 no-unit-snapshot invariant. Current stock display joins current Unit, and valuation/recipe conversions can become semantically inconsistent; no measured monetary loss or actual SQL schedule executed.
counterevidence: If movement already exists when update query runs, guard correctly rejects; selected first-movement race avoids that ordinary protection.
Receipt itself is transactional, idempotent and FK-valid; chosen nonoverlapping commits release its parent FK locks before unit update Save.
Source-account locks irrelevant to credit0 receipt and do not protect item metadata anyway.
Both actors require legitimate inventory/purchasing authority; not unauthorized privilege escalation.
No runtime queryplan/isolation/EF generated SQL observed. External serialization or unsupported metadata operation policy not certified.
source_evidence.correction_design: Coordinate Unit mutation and every first stock-posting path on same transaction-held item anchor or durable immutable-unit schema contract, recheck movement existence inside protected boundary; do not only add metadata Version if stock writers never modify parent token.
regression_tests: Barrier after unit no-movement read, commit first receipt, then metadata save must reject unit change or receipt must be admitted only under new unit with explicit semantics.
Reverse order and concurrent stock adjustment/usage paths; existing movement sequential rejection retained.
Unrelated metadata changes remain possible and same-unit updates do not fail.

evidence_chain: Authorized metadata request reads existing UnitA, no movements, passes explicit Domain unit-lock guard, pauses before Save.
